name: Receipts on the ink desk
description: Evidence prints onto a lit ink desk above his face, each line and figure landing on the word that names it, states dissolving, no camera move.

rated.words: They're all approved. I don't actually think these are the problem. I think how we integrate title cards and real-world images and motion animation is the issue.

rated_note: Krish's rating, written only by `python scripts/ve.py recipe rate <id> <score> --words "..."` ({score, by: Krish, on, words}) or `--approved` ({approved: true, by: Krish, on, words}, no score); null until he gives it. From 23 Nov 2026 ve lint uses only a recipe rated 9 or more or approved by him, or the piece's one named experiment (style.experiment) (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-19: recipes plus one named experiment slot; Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-20: all ten style combinations on the style board are approved; scripts/velib/floor.py).
generated_note: Generated (AI-made) imagery never appears in a cut (Krish, 2026-11-20), so no recipe names a generated kind and ve lint refuses any generated asset (floor.recipe_generated).
deep_dive_note: The protected baseline for a platform deep dive (Krish, 2026-11-20: "Just make sure that we don't lose the character.ai top half of the screen style ... integrate it into future videos, particularly where I deep dive into an actual platform."): the default recipe when a piece's subject is one platform, kept as it is, never restyled away. Its grammar is fade and rise, never a camera move. The devices that draw it are in deep_dive_devices; the planner reads .agents/skills/motion-designer/references/protected-baselines.md.

wordmark_header.note: the platform's registry mark only; none is a gap, never drawn type

ui_wall.note: his own screen grabs as image clips, drifting 0.6 px a frame under an ink scrim 55% to 72%

event_tape.note: items[0] the display line, items[1] the filing line (the source)

loops_on_recording.note: a mark event on the word that names each region
